title: C518 — Driver door window regulator motor
introduction:
I use this reference to connect the driver door window regulator motor’s cavity labels with the circuit descriptions below. Think of it as the window motor’s address book: supply, ground and command connections have different jobs, even though they share a housing.

Start with the connector identification table, then compare the drawing’s cavity labels with the Cavity column. Read across the matching row for its circuit, color, gauge, function and terminal information. The supply descriptions retain a fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative; this sheet does not choose between those protective devices. Repeated cavity entries and the disagreement between the metadata count and the illustrated layout remain unresolved.

This guide explains the reference, including its service-part listings. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and catalog-code meanings are not defined here. Access, probing, electrical tests, wire selection and replacement require their own instructions; these labels alone cannot establish a fault.

edits.why: The drawing places a vertical column of cavity labels on the left and separated labeled circles on the right, with a prominent housing projection above them. I use those features to navigate the illustration. The projection is not identified as a release mechanism, and the view is not explicitly identified as the mating side or wire side, so it cannot establish physical probing orientation.

Follow each cavity label across its row to distinguish fuse-or-circuit-breaker supplies, ground, window up/down commands, global-down control and the driver latch ajar signal. This separates current supply and return from information about what the window should do. Repeated up-command and down-command cavity entries have blank Qualifier fields; they do not establish whether the circuits are alternatives or share a connection. A repeated table label is not an extra hole in the housing.

I cross-reference Kit List with Number and Hard Shell with Engineering Shell to connect the identification and service tables. Service Part supplies the service identifier; Image names the associated image file. Keep the pigtail Gauge entry separate from the individual circuit Gauge entries. The listing identifies service information without teaching wire substitution, terminal installation or connector replacement.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata Pin Count conflicts with the cavity count shown by both the illustration and the pigtail Cavities entry. The supplied evidence does not reconcile them.

The up-command and down-command cavities each have differing circuit entries without configuration qualifiers. Their applicability and connection relationship require clarification before selecting a circuit.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 37 primary units, three complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. Count and repeated command-circuit applicability ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
